title: North Coast International Airport
summary: A mid-size commercial airport (terminal, FIDS, baggage handling, AODB, PA) with its Airport Emergency Plan, Airport Security Program and Terminal Incident Response Plan, and the hand-authored Scenario 3 tabletop: a manipulated AODB drives FIDS, baggage and PA to mislead passengers.
notice: EXERCISE MATERIAL — for training use. North Coast International Airport, its people and identifiers are simulated.

scenarios.title: Flight to Nowhere
scenarios.summary: A malicious actor manipulates the AODB so FIDS, baggage and PA mislead passengers; the airport must restore data integrity, manage crowds at the gates and keep public trust.

scenarios.title: Glass House
scenarios.summary: The airport's own IT Manager, extorted by a criminal syndicate, plants a rogue man-in-the-middle device to skim retail payment card data while being the most helpful person in the room; test insider threat recognition, network forensics and PCI-aware incident response.

scenarios.title: The Long Game
scenarios.summary: A cybercrime group has quietly lived inside the airport network for 90 days; the team discovers it now and must scope the damage, decide what to shut down, manage notifications, and plan recovery while keeping the airport operating.

scenarios.title: The Leak
scenarios.summary: A local TV station broadcasts details from the airport's Sensitive Security Information security program, forcing a parallel insider-leak investigation and mass security remediation while the airport keeps operating.

scenarios.title: Carbon Copy
scenarios.summary: A cloned vendor badge is used to plant a rogue wireless access point in a network infrastructure room; IT must assemble the PACS, CCTV and switch evidence to find it and decide how to contain it.

scenarios.title: Friendly Fire
scenarios.summary: Every POS terminal in the airport goes dark two minutes after the IT Manager's emergency firewall rule, while a real SSH scan and a vendor firmware push make a cyberattack and a supply-chain compromise look equally plausible.

scenarios.title: Social Engineering Olympics
scenarios.summary: Over two hours the facilitator role-plays 12 phone, email, in-person and social media contacts, 9 of them social engineering attacks and 3 legitimate, and teams must verify each one without rejecting everything.

scenarios.title: Countdown
scenarios.summary: An anonymous email names noon as the deadline; teams spend a 180-minute time budget on an action menu to find an ex-contractor's logic bomb on the AODB server before 12:00.
